# s321 — add-pass counts the items already in the pass

`slicer prose add-pass KEY` says how many items already sit in the pass it declares, instead of always saying "no items yet".

**Findings:** dogfooding 2026-10-16: add-pass said no items yet with s312 already in v1.14 · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:** declaring a pass automatically from `set --pass` or `add --pass`; the warning text of `set`.

## Why

On 2026-10-16 `slicer set s312 --pass v1.14` warned that v1.14 was not declared and suggested `slicer prose add-pass v1.14 --after <pass>`. Following that hint printed `created pass v1.14 (no items yet); file items with slicer add --pass v1.14`, but s312 was already in it. The text is a fixed string (`cmd_prose_add_pass`, `src/slicer/cli.py:2784`), so it is wrong exactly on the path slicer's own warning recommends.

## Files

- `src/slicer/cli.py`, `cmd_prose_add_pass`: count `state.index.items` whose `pass_key` is the new key. With none, keep today's line. With some, print `created pass KEY for N existing item(s)`, without the "file items with" hint. The JSON payload is unchanged.
- `CHANGELOG.md` under Fixed.
- `tests/test_prose.py`.
